query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a gradient hierarchical microstructure through tailored thermo-mechanical processing can improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies
generation.intervention: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing to create a gradient hierarchical microstructure
generation.mechanism: Two-hierarchical constraint effect and self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism
generation.boundary: Limited to eutectic high-entropy alloys with specific composition and microstructure
generation.uncertainty: The exact processing parameters and microstructural features required to achieve optimal strength-ductility synergy are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical properties of eutectic high-entropy alloys with and without gradient hierarchical microstructure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with gradient hierarchical microstructure does not show improved strength-ductility synergy compared to the unmodified alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Enhanced strength–ductility synergy in ultrafine-grained eutectic high-entropy alloys by inheriting microstructural lamellae

Abstract: Realizing improved strength–ductility synergy in eutectic alloys acting as in situ composite materials remains a challenge in conventional eutectic systems, which is why eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs), a newly-emerging multi-principal-element eutectic category, may offer wider in situ composite possibilities. Here, we use an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA to engineer an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that deliberately inherits its composite lamellar nature by tailored thermo-mechanical processing to achieve property combinations which are not accessible to previously-reported reinforcement methodologies.
